morphology.name: Avulsion Fracture
morphology.plain: A ligament or tendon pulls a bone fragment off.
morphology.common_bones: Malleoli, phalanges, pelvic apophyses, tibial tubercle

morphology.name: Comminuted Fracture
morphology.plain: Bone broken into three or more pieces.
morphology.common_bones: Tibia, femur, humerus, calcaneus after high energy

morphology.name: Fracture-Dislocation
morphology.plain: Break plus the joint is out of place.

morphology.name: Greenstick Fracture
morphology.plain: Incomplete break in a flexible (usually paediatric) bone.

morphology.name: Hairline Fracture
morphology.plain: Very thin crack; easy to miss on X-ray.

morphology.name: Impacted Fracture
morphology.plain: Fragments are driven into each other.
morphology.common_bones: Proximal humerus, femoral neck, distal radius

morphology.name: Longitudinal Fracture
morphology.plain: Crack runs along the long axis of the bone.

morphology.name: Pathological Fracture
morphology.plain: Break through bone weakened by disease (tumour, osteoporosis, cyst).

morphology.name: Spiral Fracture
morphology.plain: Helical break from a twisting force.
